questions.q: What does Lakehouse Monitoring add on top of row filters, column masks, and audit logs?
options: It profiles a table on a schedule and generates a dashboard, showing whether data quality and access patterns hold up over time
It replaces the need for Unity Catalog grants entirely
It automatically deletes tables that fail a quality check
It is only used for billing, not data quality
questions.explain: Monitoring answers whether the controls set up elsewhere are still working over time — row filters and masks set the rule, monitoring checks the ongoing result.

questions.q: Where does a monitored table's generated dashboard appear, besides its own Quality tab in Catalog Explorer?
options: In the workspace's general Dashboards list, like any other dashboard
It is only viewable through the REST API, never in the UI
Only in the account console, not in any workspace
It does not persist anywhere — it's regenerated fresh each time you click View dashboard
questions.explain: The generated dashboard is an ordinary dashboard object, so it also shows up in the workspace's Dashboards list alongside any other dashboard — filterable and shareable the same way.

questions.q: What happens when you click Refresh on a monitoring dashboard?
options: It re-runs the dashboard's queries over the already-computed metric tables — it does not trigger a new profile calculation
It immediately re-profiles the entire table from scratch
It deletes the dashboard and regenerates it from a template
It has no effect unless the underlying table has been renamed
questions.explain: Refreshing the dashboard only reruns its queries over existing metric data. To get new underlying numbers, you must refresh the monitor itself (via UI, API, or schedule) first.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what connects classification, auditing, lineage, and monitoring into one answerable compliance question?
options: A shared compliance framework label (e.g. GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS) applied across these tools
A single REST API endpoint that queries all four at once automatically
They are not connected — each tool must be checked independently with no shared reference point
A single governed tag called 'compliance' that must be manually applied to every object
questions.explain: The same compliance-framework label used in classification results ties together which data is classified, who accessed it, where it flows, and whether exposure is trending up or down — turning a one-time audit into a standing, answerable question.

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe governance as 'a continuous practice, not a one-time setup'?
options: Because controls like row filters and tags only establish rules — monitoring is needed to confirm those rules are still holding as data and access patterns change
Because Unity Catalog permissions automatically expire every 30 days
Because Databricks requires governance policies to be re-submitted for approval monthly
Because row filters and column masks stop working after a fixed retention period
questions.explain: Setting up a row filter, tag, or policy is a point-in-time action; monitoring (and the compliance-framework view across the chapter's tools) is what verifies those controls are still effective on an ongoing basis.
